{
  "hypothesis": "Predicted that temporal selection during the attentional blink would vary along three dissociable dimensions—efficacy (suppression), latency (delay), and precision (diffusion)—exhibiting distinct time courses across stimulus onset asynchrony levels.",
  "design": "within-subjects, with factors of T1 onset (5 levels) and T1-T2 SOA (10 levels)",
  "manipulation_or_predictor": "Stimulus onset asynchrony (SOA) between two targets (T1 and T2) in a rapid serial visual presentation stream",
  "outcome_measure": "Distribution of reported letter serial positions, yielding measures of efficacy, center of mass (latency), and variance (precision) around the target",
  "population_and_setting": "Twelve participants between the ages of 18 and 35 recruited from the Massachusetts Institute of Technology subject pool",
  "sample_size_total": 12,
  "recruitment_and_incentive": "Recruited from the MIT subject pool, paid a flat rate of $10 plus performance-based bonus cash awards ($0.01 for each letter reported correctly)",
  "analysis_plan": "Analysis of variance with factors of SOA, measure, and target, followed by pair-wise t-tests comparing the time courses of the three effects across subjects",
  "preregistered_or_confirmatory": "not stated",
  "other_methods_notes": "Participants completed 4 blocks of 100 trials each following 2 practice trials. Each trial featured an RSVP stream of 26 letters presented at 12 items/s, with two annulus cues indicating target letters."
}
